title: Linkability of GPS data to child identity
description: Regular GPS coordinate transmissions can be linked to identify the specific child and correlate with other data sources, enabling tracking of the child's movements over time.
assumptions: GPS data contains sufficient precision to identify individual children

title: Identifiability through location data
description: Live GPS coordinates can directly identify the child's current location, home address, school, and daily routines, creating a detailed location profile.
assumptions: GPS coordinates are precise enough to identify specific locations

title: Unauthorized disclosure of GPS coordinates
description: GPS data transmitted to the backend could be intercepted during transmission or accessed by unauthorized parties at the backend, exposing the child's location.
assumptions: Transmission may not be fully encrypted or backend may have insufficient access controls

title: Aggregation of location data for profiling
description: Regular GPS transmissions can be aggregated to build comprehensive movement profiles, revealing patterns about the child's habits, routines, and social connections.
assumptions: Backend stores and processes historical GPS data

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: The child or guardians may not be fully aware of the frequency, purpose, or extent of GPS data collection and how it will be used or shared.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain continuous location tracking

title: Non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Collection of children's location data may violate regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K if proper consent, data minimization, and parental controls are not implemented.
assumptions: Backend processes data from minors without appropriate safeguards
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Location pings can be linked to identify individual movement patterns
description: Location history data written to the store can be linked across time to reconstruct an individual's movement patterns, habits, and routines, enabling profiling and tracking.
assumptions: Location data includes timestamps and coordinates that can be correlated

title: Location data can directly identify individuals
description: Location history is highly identifying personal data that can reveal home addresses, workplaces, and sensitive locations, potentially identifying specific individuals.
assumptions: Location data is stored with user identifiers or can be linked to user accounts

title: Unauthorized access to location history store
description: If the Location History Store is compromised or accessed without authorization, sensitive location data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data store has access controls that could be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Excessive collection of location data
description: The system may be collecting more location data than necessary (e.g., continuous tracking vs. on-demand), violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Location pings are written for each event without clear necessity justification
uncertainty_note: Depends on business requirements and data retention policies

title: Users unaware of location data storage
description: Users may not be fully aware that their location pings are being stored in a persistent data store, or the extent of this storage.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate location data storage practices

title: Location data linking across sessions
description: Location pings forwarded to the Geofencing Engine could be linked across multiple sessions to build comprehensive movement profiles of users, enabling correlation of user activities over time.
assumptions: Geofencing Engine stores or processes historical location data

title: User identification through location patterns
description: Location data transmitted to the Geofencing Engine could enable identification of specific users based on their unique movement patterns, zone entry/exit times, and location history.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals

title: Excessive location data disclosure
description: The flow may disclose more location data than necessary for geofencing purposes. Full location pings might be sent when only zone boundary crossing information is needed, violating data minimality.
assumptions: Backend sends complete location coordinates rather than just zone-crossing events
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether backend sends full coordinates or just zone-crossing events

title: User unawareness of geofencing data processing
description: Users may not be aware that their location data is being processed by a separate Geofencing Engine for zone monitoring, beyond the basic location tracking they consented to.
assumptions: Privacy policy does not clearly explain geofencing data flows

title: Unauthorized access to location data in transit
description: Location pings transmitted between Backend and Geofencing Engine could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured.
assumptions: Internal network security may have vulnerabilities

title: Unauthorized disclosure of zone definitions
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house locations) stored in the Family Account Store could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data store is compromised or the data flow is intercepted. This reveals sensitive location information about family members.
assumptions: Data store has appropriate access controls; flow is protected in transit

title: Location profile aggregation
description: Zone definitions from multiple family members could be aggregated to build detailed location profiles, revealing patterns of movement, associations, and daily routines. This flow contributes to the data aggregation that enables such profiling.
assumptions: Multiple zone definitions exist for different family members

title: Identifiable location data exposure
description: Zone definitions like 'home', 'school', and 'friend's house' can identify specific locations associated with family members. If these zones are specific enough (e.g., exact addresses), they could directly identify individuals and their personal locations.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain specific location identifiers

title: Unawareness of location data access
description: Family members may be unaware that their configured zone definitions are being read by the Geofencing Engine, or may not understand the implications of this data access for their privacy and location tracking.
assumptions: Users have not been fully informed about data flows

title: Location data linkable to child identity
description: Geofencing notifications sent to the parent link the child's location movements (zone entry/exit events) to their identity, creating a persistent link between location data and personal identity.
assumptions: Notifications contain or can be correlated with child identification information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location notifications
description: Location-based arrival/departure notifications could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission from the Geofencing Engine to the parent.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully secured

title: Location data aggregation over time
description: Multiple geofencing notifications over time can be aggregated to build a detailed profile of the child's movement patterns, habits, and routines.
assumptions: Notifications are stored or logged by the parent or system

title: Child unaware of location monitoring
description: The child may not be aware that their location is being monitored and that notifications are being sent to the parent when they enter or exit defined zones.
assumptions: Child may not have been informed about the geofencing system

title: Direct Identifiability of Parent and Child
description: Parent registration data includes directly identifying information (name, DOB, school) that can uniquely identify both the parent and child. This data is transmitted from the external entity to the backend process.
assumptions: Standard registration flow with personal data collection

title: Linkability of Family Data
description: Registration data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) can be linked to other data about the family across different systems or over time, creating a comprehensive profile.
assumptions: Data may be stored and correlated with other app usage data

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Profile Data
description: Child profile information (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or if the backend is compromised.
assumptions: Data transmitted over network and stored in backend systems

title: Data Aggregation Revealing Family Patterns
description: Registration data combined with other app usage data (location tracking, activity logs) could reveal detailed patterns about family routines, school schedules, and home locations.
assumptions: App collects additional data beyond initial registration

title: Non-compliance with Children's Privacy Regulations
description: Collection of children's personal data (name, DOB, school, location) may violate regulations like COPPA if proper parental consent mechanisms and data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: App operates in jurisdiction with children's privacy laws
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation of consent mechanisms

title: Linkability of child profiles to accounts and locations
description: Child profile data stored in DS2 can be linked to specific family accounts and geofence zones, enabling correlation of children's identities with their locations and family relationships.
assumptions: Data store maintains relationships between account IDs, child profiles, and geofence zones

title: Identifiability of children through stored profile data
description: Child profile data stored in DS2 may contain or enable identification of individual children, especially when combined with account and geofence information.
assumptions: Child profiles contain personally identifiable information or can be linked to real identities

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored personal data
description: Account, child profile, and geofence zone data stored in DS2 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Data store has security controls that could be compromised

title: Excessive data collection beyond minimality principle
description: The backend may store more account, child profile, or geofence data than strictly necessary for the application's functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Data collection scope exceeds what is required for core functionality
uncertainty_note: Cannot verify exact data fields stored without schema details

title: User unawareness of data storage practices
description: Users may not be fully aware of what account, child profile, and geofence data is being stored, how long it is retained, or what purposes it serves.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data storage practices

title: Limited user control over stored personal data
description: Users may have limited ability to access, modify, or delete their account, child profile, and geofence data stored in DS2.
assumptions: Data management interfaces may not provide full CRUD capabilities

title: Location data linkability across time
description: Multiple location requests from the parent can be linked to create comprehensive movement patterns and routines of the child, enabling inference of sensitive information about daily activities, habits, and locations visited.
assumptions: Location data is stored and can be correlated across multiple requests

title: Child identifiability through location data
description: Location data is inherently tied to a specific child's identity, and the parent's access to this data confirms the child's identity within the system. This could enable tracking and identification of the child's whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is associated with child identity in the backend

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: Location data transmitted from parent to backend or stored in the backend could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties through network attacks, backend vulnerabilities, or insider threats.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage may have security vulnerabilities

title: Location data aggregation for profiling
description: Multiple location requests over time can be aggregated to build detailed location profiles of the child, revealing patterns, routines, and sensitive locations that could be misused.
assumptions: Location history is stored and can be aggregated

title: Child unawareness of location sharing
description: The child may be unaware that their location data is being shared with the parent through this flow, or may not understand the extent of location tracking and data processing.
assumptions: Child consent or awareness mechanisms may be insufficient

title: GDPR/regulatory compliance for location data
description: Location data is considered sensitive personal data under GDPR and similar regulations. Processing this data requires proper legal basis, consent, and data protection measures that may not be fully implemented.
assumptions: Location data processing must comply with privacy regulations

title: Location history linkable to specific children
description: Location history data stored in DS1 can be linked to identify specific children through movement patterns, home/school locations, and routine behaviors. When retrieved by the backend, this linkability enables profiling of individual children.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals through pattern analysis

title: Location data enables child identification
description: Stored location history is inherently identifying data that can reveal who a child is, where they live, attend school, and their daily routines. Retrieval of this data by the backend makes it available for identification purposes.
assumptions: Location history contains sufficient detail to identify individual children

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location history
description: If the backend (P1) or data store (DS1) is compromised, or if access controls are insufficient, location history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties. This is particularly sensitive given it involves children's location data.
assumptions: Backend and data store have potential security vulnerabilities or access control gaps

title: Location data aggregation reveals sensitive patterns
description: Aggregating location history over time can reveal sensitive patterns about family routines, school schedules, medical appointments, and other private activities. The backend retrieval enables this aggregation for parent viewing.
assumptions: Location history is stored with sufficient temporal granularity to enable pattern analysis

title: Parents unaware of location data usage scope
description: Parents may not be fully aware of the extent of location data being retrieved and displayed, including historical depth, precision, or how the data is being used beyond the map/history view.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate the full scope of location data retrieval and usage

title: Potential non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Retrieving and displaying children's location history may violate regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other children's privacy laws if proper consent, data minimization, and security measures are not in place.
assumptions: Location data of children is subject to enhanced privacy protections under applicable regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Linkability between parent, secondary guardian, and child
description: The invitation flow creates linkability between the parent (EE1), the secondary guardian being invited, and the child whose location is being shared. This enables correlation of identities and activities across multiple parties.
assumptions: The invitation contains identifiers that can link these parties together

title: Direct identification of parent and secondary guardian
description: The parent's identity and the secondary guardian's identity are transmitted to the backend, making both parties directly identifiable in the system.
assumptions: Identity information is included in the invitation request

title: Disclosure of child location access permissions
description: The backend processes and stores information about who has access to the child's location data, which could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if not properly secured.
assumptions: Access permission data is stored in the backend

title: Unawareness of data processing by secondary guardian
description: The secondary guardian may not be fully aware of how their identity and access permissions are being processed and stored by the backend system.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data processing for secondary guardians

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Sharing child location data with secondary guardians may require specific consent mechanisms under regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K, which may not be properly implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for child location sharing apply to this system
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation

title: Linkability of child's location data
description: The backend sharing live location data with the secondary guardian enables linking the child's location across time periods and potentially with other data sources, creating a comprehensive movement profile.
assumptions: Location data is shared in a format that can be correlated over time

title: Identifiability through location data
description: Live location data shared with the secondary guardian can be used to identify the child, especially when combined with other contextual information or when the location is unique.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient precision to identify the child

title: Unauthorized disclosure to secondary guardian
description: The backend may disclose the child's location to the secondary guardian without proper authorization verification, or the secondary guardian may lack adequate security controls to protect the data.
assumptions: Secondary guardian is an external entity outside the system boundary with potentially weaker security controls

title: Child unaware of location sharing
description: The child may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, violating transparency principles and potentially consent requirements.
assumptions: Children may not have capacity to understand or consent to location sharing

title: Non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Sharing children's location data with external entities may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws requiring parental consent and data minimization.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with children's privacy protections

title: Linkability of aggregated analytics to user profiles
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with the advertising partner may be linkable to individual user profiles when combined with other data sources the partner possesses, enabling cross-service tracking and profiling.
assumptions: Advertising/analytics partners typically maintain extensive user profiles and may attempt to link incoming analytics data to existing profiles.

title: Re-identification from aggregated analytics data
description: Even aggregated analytics data may allow re-identification of individual users through statistical inference, especially when combined with other datasets or when aggregation groups are small.
assumptions: The aggregation level may not be sufficient to prevent re-identification attacks, and the partner may have access to complementary datasets.

title: Unauthorized disclosure to third parties
description: The advertising/analytics partner may disclose or share the received analytics data with additional third parties beyond the original agreement, expanding the data's reach without user consent.
assumptions: External partners may have their own data-sharing practices that extend beyond the initial data flow agreement.

title: User unawareness of analytics data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their usage and engagement data is being shared with external advertising partners, violating transparency expectations.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly communicate the extent of data sharing with third-party analytics partners.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in cross-border data sharing
description: Sharing analytics data with external partners may violate privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) if proper consent, data protection agreements, or cross-border transfer mechanisms are not in place.
assumptions: The advertising partner may be located in a different jurisdiction with different privacy requirements.

title: Location data linkability to child identity
description: The child's location data sent in check-in/SOS messages can be linked to their identity and combined with other data flows to create a comprehensive movement profile of the child.
assumptions: Child's identity is known to the system and location data is stored/processed

title: Direct identifiability from check-in messages
description: The manual check-in/SOS message with location is directly attributable to a specific child, making them fully identifiable from this data flow.
assumptions: System maintains association between messages and child accounts

title: Attributable data evidence for child actions
description: The check-in/SOS message can be used as evidence that the child sent it, potentially creating non-repudiation issues if the child disputes sending the message or if it was sent accidentally.
assumptions: Message metadata includes sender identification and timestamp

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child location data
description: If the Mobile App Backend is compromised or has inadequate access controls, the child's sensitive location data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Backend stores or processes location data with potential access vulnerabilities

title: Location data aggregation revealing movement patterns
description: Multiple check-in/SOS messages over time can be aggregated to reveal the child's movement patterns, routines, and frequently visited locations beyond what was intended.
assumptions: System retains historical location data from multiple check-ins

title: Child unawareness of location data implications
description: The child may not fully understand the privacy implications of sending location data, especially in emergency SOS contexts where they may not consider long-term data retention.
assumptions: Child users may lack full comprehension of data collection scope

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Collecting and processing location data from children may violate regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with child privacy protections
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details
